To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the total radiation exposure in Crohn’s patients has increased over the years.

the total ionizing radiation exposure is increasing over time in Crohn’s patients and that the main risk factors for high exposure are penetrating phenotype, abdominal surgery and steroid resistance, and immunosuppressive treatment with azathioprine or anti-TNF- α.

the cumulative effective dose of radiations is still increasing in our patients with CD, that patients with penetrating CD and those who underwent abdominal surgery were exposed earlier on in the course of the diseases to high doses, that the use of immunomodulators and anti-TNF therapy was predictive factors of higher radiation exposure, and that the value of cumulative effective dose increased in the first years of immunosuppressive therapy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the risk of cancer and other late effects of ionizing radiation in patients with CD, and it is important to identify the risk factors for high CDR.
the fact that CD patients undergo high-radiation exposure, and this should be a concern for clinicians, radiologists, and health care providers.
a population of CD patients that is exposed to ionizing radiation in a higher extent than previously thought.

the medical profession should be blamed for the increasing exposure of CD patients to ionizing radiation, as the radiological procedures have not been optimized and the number of examinations has increased over the years.
the risk factors for radiation exposure in CD are mainly the disease itself and the treatment of the disease.
the medical community is still increasing the radiation exposure of CD patients, with a significant risk of developing malignancies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ionizing radiation exposure is increasing over time, and the patients should be informed about it.
the radiation exposure of our CD patients is still increasing and that the responsibility of this fact is shared between physicians and pharmaceutical companies.
the risk for radiation exposure is still present and increasing in CD, and that it is mainly related to the disease activity and treatment.

the cumulative effective dose of ionizing radiation is still increasing in patients with CD.

physicians should be aware of the risk of radiation exposure, especially in patients with penetrating CD, and that they should be careful when using radiological imaging, especially in young patients, and should avoid unnecessary radiological studies.
the radiation burden of patients with CD is increasing and that physicians should be more careful with radiation exposure, especially in young patients.
